name: Anguilla

legalStatuses.label: Sole trader (registered business)
legalStatuses.plain: You run the business as an individual under your own name or a business name. You and the business are the same person for tax. Usually the simplest way to start.
legalStatuses.feeNote: You apply for a business licence (Form A) to the Ministry of Economic Development, then register and pay at the Inland Revenue Department. The fee depends on your activity.

legalStatuses.label: Limited company
legalStatuses.plain: The company is its own legal person, separate from you. It costs more to set up and has more paperwork, but it can limit your personal risk.
legalStatuses.feeNote: A company costs more to set up than a sole trader business. The Commercial Registry quotes the current fees.

launchSteps.label: Choose your business name and check that it is free
Incorporate the company at the Commercial Registry
launchSteps.plain: Only needed for a limited company.

launchSteps.label: Apply for your business licence
launchSteps.plain: Fill in Form A for the Ministry of Economic Development. When it is approved, register and pay at the Inland Revenue Department. The fee depends on the activity.

launchSteps.label: Register with the Social Security Board
launchSteps.plain: Self-employed people must register and contribute. The Interim Stabilisation Levy is filed with the Inland Revenue Department.

launchSteps.label: Open a separate bank account for the business
launchSteps.plain: Keeping business money apart from household money makes your numbers clearer and your taxes easier to pay.

launchSteps.label: Register as an employer and prepare payroll payments
launchSteps.plain: With employees you pay Social Security and the Interim Stabilisation Levy every month.

launchSteps.label: Register for GST
launchSteps.plain: Required when your taxable sales reach EC$300,000 in twelve months, or when you expect them to. Apply within 15 days.

contributions.label: Social Security
contributions.plain: Social Security gives access to a pension and other benefits. Self-employed people pay 8% of their income, up to EC$7,000 a month.

contributions.label: Interim Stabilisation Levy
contributions.plain: A levy on earnings: self-employed people pay 6% on the part of their earnings above EC$2,000 a month.

vat.label: Goods and Services Tax
vat.registerNote: Register within 15 days of reaching the threshold, or if you expect to reach it within twelve months. Short-term accommodation, auctioneers and public entertainment providers register from their first day.
vat.filingNote: GST returns are filed every month, by the 20th of the following month.

calendar.monthlyText: If registered for GST: file your return by the 20th of the following month. With employees: pay Social Security and the Interim Stabilisation Levy.
calendar.annualTextPersonal: Renew your business licence with the Inland Revenue Department.
calendar.payrollText: Every month: pay Social Security and the Interim Stabilisation Levy for the previous month.
calendar.vatText: If you are registered for GST: file your return every month, by the 20th of the following month.

notes: Anguilla has no income tax and no corporate tax. Your main costs are Social Security, the Interim Stabilisation Levy and, above EC$300,000 in sales, the 13% GST.
toVerify: Business licence fee for your activity
